ask: Good answer: specific amount (RWF or USD), specific use breakdown (e.g. 40% product, 30% team, 20% marketing, 10% ops), runway it buys (months). Flag: round-number ask with no use breakdown, or runway longer than 24 months.
business_registration: Good answer: names the legal entity type (sole proprietor, partnership, Ltd, cooperative, NGO), registration body (RDB for Rwanda), and registration number or status (registered / in progress). For licenses, names the regulator (e.g. BNR for fintech, NAEB for agri export). Flag: "we will register" with no timeline.
cap_table: Good answer: lists every shareholder with percentage. Percentages sum to 100. ESOP is named separately if it exists. If multiple share classes, says so. Flag: percentages do not sum to 100, or single "100% founders" with no founder names.
competition_and_edge: Good answer: names 2-4 real competitors (companies that actually exist, by name) and one differentiator per. "No competition" is almost always wrong — substitutes count. Flag: only generic names like "informal sellers".
compliance: Good answer: names sector regulators that apply (RRA for tax — applies to everyone; BNR for fintech; NAEB for agri-export; RICA for telecoms; RMA for medical; MINEDUC for edtech). Confirms tax registration with RRA. If cross-border, names which countries and which compliance regimes. Flag: "we are compliant" without naming any regulator.
contracts: Good answer: lists what's in place — founder agreement, employment or contractor agreements, supplier or customer contracts, NDAs. Says which are signed vs in-progress vs missing. Flag: "we have agreements" with no specifics.
discovery: Good answer: at least 5-10 customer conversations with named quotes or grouped insights. Numbers of people, where, how (in-person, phone, survey). Flag: vague "customers told us" without count.
features: Good answer: current features as a short list and next 2-3 features with a rough timeframe. Flag: feature list reads like a wish list with no priority.
financial_history: Good answer: total spent to date with rough breakdown (product, team, marketing, ops). Source of funds (bootstrapped, grant, family). Currency consistent (prefer RWF). Flag: numbers given without a time window.
gtm_strategy: Good answer: names channels (USSD, WhatsApp, agent network, cooperatives, schools, churches — whatever fits). Pricing model named (subscription, transaction fee, freemium). For Rwanda specifically: mobile money is a normal channel; partnerships with cooperatives or SACCOs are normal acquisition paths. Flag: "social media marketing" alone without specifics.
impact_metrics: Good answer: numbers, with a time window. Users served, jobs created, % income change, SDG alignment if relevant. Quote sources where applicable. For impact-aligned investors in East Africa, this is one of the most important sections. Flag: stories instead of measurements, or unverifiable claims.
ip: Good answer: lists IP assets (trademark, copyright, patent, trade secret, software code) and protection status. For Rwanda, trademark filings go through ORIPI (formerly OPIC). Flag: "we own the IP" without saying which IP or how it's protected.
market_size: Good answer: separates TAM, SAM, SOM with at least one source (NISR, World Bank Rwanda, sector report). For Rwanda, common sources: NISR (statistics), MINAGRI (agriculture), BNR (finance), MINEDUC (education). Flag: round numbers with no source, or SOM > 5% of SAM Year 1.
marketing_assets: Good answer: lists what exists (brand kit, one-pager, flyer, social posts, demo video). Upload should match. Flag: claims many assets but uploads are empty.
name: C4E Data Room Hint
narrative: Good answer: one sentence. Memorable. Specific. The line the investor repeats to a colleague. Under 25 words. Flag: generic phrases ("changing the future of X", "empowering Y").
partnerships: Good answer: signed agreements only (MoU, LOI, pilot contract). Name the partner, date, scope. If logos used, says permission granted. Flag: verbal interest treated as a partnership.
problem: Good answer: names a specific group ("smallholder farmers in Northern Province"), describes one concrete pain ("lose 30-50% of harvest income"), and gives one source (interview count, survey, statistic with citation). Flag: speculation without evidence.
projections: Good answer: 3-year revenue and cost projection with stated assumptions (price per unit, units sold, growth rate). Currency consistent. For Rwanda agritech / fintech, healthy growth assumptions are 30-100% Year 2 and Year 3, not 1000%. Flag: hockey-stick projection with no assumptions.
stage: Good answer: names one of idea, prototype, MVP, pilot, launched, scaling. For pilot or beyond, gives a count (users, transactions, deployments). Flag: "we are building" with no specifics.
testimonials: Good answer: real quotes from named or anonymised real customers. Permission noted. Flag: quotes that read like marketing copy.
testing: Good answer: real users, number of them, period tested, what changed as a result. Flag: "we got positive feedback" with no specifics.
traction: Good answer: numbers. Users, paying customers, transactions, revenue, retention. With a time window ("in the last 3 months"). Flag: vanity metrics only (Instagram followers, app downloads with no usage).
unit_economics: Good answer: CAC (or rough estimate), revenue per customer, gross margin, payback period. For pre-revenue ventures, projected unit economics with stated assumptions. Flag: LTV/CAC > 5 in Year 1 with no traction (almost always wrong).
uvp: Good answer: one sentence that says what you do, for whom, and why it's better. Avoid "the only" or "the first" unless verifiable. Flag: same as competition (if UVP is just "we are better").
